evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

scope_limitation.statement: The coupled-scenario definition (roster membership, champion identities, levels, builds, fight window) is NOT reachable from the permitted evidence tree. It lives in scripts/golden_snapshot.py, which runbook R-18/R-19 forbids me to read; data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json contains no coupled scenarios and no scenario named cleaver_bloodsong_roster (searched: 22 scenario ids, zero hits for 'Bloodsong', 'Cleaver', 'coupled', 'roster').
scope_limitation.consequence: A bit-exact end-to-end re-simulation of this leaf is impossible from data/ + docs/math-foundations.md alone. What IS decidable from the permitted sources is which of the two candidate values is reachable from the cached wiki text and the doc's own closed forms, and which one is only reachable from the un-refined model the doc explicitly labels an approximation. That is the test I ran.

sources_quoted.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.

the established model uses a fixed `0.8*max_stacks` constant (with a `hits/2` short-fight branch). Under the engine's own ordering convention (4 leading ability hits apply stacks before the auto stream) the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp `min(k, C)` over `h` hits is `C - C(C-1)/(2h)` for `h >= C` ... the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +/-20% at the extremes ... Recommendation: replace the constant with the closed-form Cesaro mean
actual_damage = raw * 100 / (100 + resistance); R_final = max(0, (R - r_flat)*(1 - r_pct/100)*(1 - p) - f)
`f(S)` = the coupled participant-timeline score: deterministic total damage dealt by the main participant before its own death, summed over the fight window
sources_quoted.why: Fixes the meaning of the leaf: '.../combat/objective/main_team_damage_before_death' is the coupled objective block (damage before death), not a fight against an epic monster. Nothing in data/ models dragons/baron, which corroborates this reading.

sources_quoted.quote: Ravenous Hydra / Tiamat 'Cleave' {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}; Blade of the Ruined King {{rd|9%|6%}}; World Atlas 'Shared Riches' minion execute {{rd|50%|30%}}
sources_quoted.why: Confirms {{rd|A|B}} = A for a melee holder, B for a ranged holder. So Bloodsong's Expose Weakness is 8% for a melee holder and 5% for a ranged holder - it is NOT a single constant.

sources_quoted.quote: Bloodsong Spellblade atom values [10.0, 100.0, 4.0, 8.0, 5.0, 1.5] units [s, percent, s, percent, percent, flat]; Black Cleaver Carve atom values [6.0, 5.0, 6.0, 30.0, 5.0]
sources_quoted.why: The parsed atom layer carries BOTH 8 and 5 for Expose Weakness, i.e. the split is present in the machine-readable cache too.

independent_computation.method: Because the scenario spec is out of scope, I inverted the leaf: I solved, for each wiki-sourced correction that the cache/doc supports, the single free parameter it needs, and checked whether that parameter lands in a physically plausible range. A correction that reproduces the new value only with an absurd parameter would indict it; one that reproduces it with an ordinary parameter supports it. Two independent corrections were tested; both reproduce 4041.9 with ordinary parameters, and neither can produce 4074.9.

reconstruction_1_expose_weakness_melee_r.rule: S1 + S6: Expose Weakness amplifies all sources by 8% (melee holder) / 5% (ranged holder) for 4 s. A model that hardcodes the melee 8% over-credits every ranged holder.
reconstruction_1_expose_weakness_melee_r.algebra: T = U + A*(1 + a), where A = team damage dealt inside Expose Weakness windows measured pre-amplification, U = damage outside the windows. Correcting a: 8% -> 5% gives dT = -A*(0.08 - 0.05) = -0.03*A.
reconstruction_1_expose_weakness_melee_r.plausibility: A/(U + A) = 1100.0/3986.9 = 27.6% of the fight's raw damage falling inside the 4 s debuff windows - an ordinary uptime share for a 4 s debuff re-applied on a 1.5 s Spellblade cooldown in a short coupled fight.
reconstruction_1_expose_weakness_melee_r.residual: Whether 8% or 5% is right depends on the Bloodsong holder being melee or ranged - the one input I cannot see. If the holder is melee, this reconstruction indicts the change instead. See falsifier.

reconstruction_2_black_cleaver_cesaro_me.rule: S2 + S3: Carve is 6% armor reduction per stack, cap 5 stacks / 30%. The doc's exact average over a fight of h stack-applying hits is stacks = C - C(C-1)/(2h) = 5 - 10/h, against the established fixed constant 0.8*C = 4.00 stacks (24%).
reconstruction_2_black_cleaver_cesaro_me.direction_test: 5 - 10/h < 4  <=>  h < 10. So the Cesaro correction LOWERS damage exactly when the fight is shorter than ~10 stack-applying hits, which matches the observed sign.
reconstruction_2_black_cleaver_cesaro_me.worked_example: h = 8 hits -> stacks 3.75 -> reduction 22.5% (vs 24%). Target armor R: effective armor 0.76R -> 0.775R (S4: reduction applies before penetration; multiplier m = 100/(100+R_eff)).
reconstruction_2_black_cleaver_cesaro_me.plausibility: R ~ 93 armor is an ordinary level-18 target armor, and h = 8 an ordinary short coupled fight. Neighbouring armors bracket the answer tightly: R=80 -> 4044.7, R=90 -> 4042.5, R=100 -> 4040.5, R=110 -> 4038.6. Every value in the plausible armor band reproduces the new value to within ~0.1%, and none of them reproduces the old value.
reconstruction_2_black_cleaver_cesaro_me.note: This reconstruction assumes the leaf's damage is dominated by armor-mitigated physical damage, which a Black Cleaver + Bloodsong (100% base AD physical Spellblade) roster is.

independent_computation.why_the_old_value_is_not_reachable: 4074.9 is reachable only from the un-refined readings: a flat 8% Expose Weakness with no melee/ranged split (contradicted by S1/S6/S7), and/or the fixed 0.8*max_stacks Black Cleaver constant that S3 itself labels 'a documented tuning constant, not a theorem' with a standing recommendation to replace it by the closed form. No reading of the cached wiki text produces a value ABOVE 4041.9 that the sources justify: every wiki-grounded refinement of this scenario's two effects (champion-only gating of Expose Weakness, the ranged 5% branch, the 1.5 s Spellblade cooldown, the 4 s debuff window, the exact Cesaro stack mean in a sub-10-hit fight) moves the number DOWN, and the observed move is down by 0.81%.
independent_computation.sanity_bounds: Full removal of an 8% Expose Weakness from the entire fight would cost ~302 damage (4074.9 - 4074.9/1.08 = 301.9); full removal of Black Cleaver's 24% shred at R~93 would cost ~9-10%. The observed -33.0 is ~11% of the first bound and well inside the second - i.e. the change is a refinement of one term, not a structural rewrite, which is consistent with a single sourced-parameter correction and inconsistent with an effect being dropped wholesale.

falsifier.statement: Reconstruction 1 flips sign if and only if the Bloodsong holder in this roster is a MELEE champion, in which case 8% is the correct branch of {{rd|8%|5%}} and the old 4074.9 would be right.
falsifier.how_to_settle: Read the roster of coupled scenario 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' in the golden snapshot definition and check the Bloodsong holder's attack type in data/champions.json. That file is outside this oracle's permitted evidence tree; a reviewer with access can settle it in one look.
falsifier.residual_risk: If instead the change restricted Expose Weakness to the holder's own damage, that would contradict S1's 'increased damage from all sources' and would also lower the number - this is the one wiki-contradicting way to reach 4041.9. Reconstruction 1's solved slice (A = 1100.0, 27.6% of raw) is a whole-team-sized slice rather than a support-sized one, which argues against that failure mode but does not exclude it.

verdict_rationale: Two independent, separately sourced corrections - the Bloodsong {{rd|8%|5%}} melee/ranged split (data/items.json id 3877) and the Black Cleaver exact Cesaro stack mean (docs/math-foundations.md 2.3.2, C - C(C-1)/(2h)) - each reproduce 4041.9 from 4074.9 with ordinary, physically plausible parameters (a 27.6% debuff-window damage share; ~93 target armor over an 8-hit fight). The old value corresponds in both cases to the coarser model that the cached wiki text and the doc's own closed form supersede. I therefore accept the new value, with the melee/ranged roster fact recorded above as the single unchecked input.
